Parking the whole roadmap. Here is what I'll do, written as the tool calls I'd run. Nothing has run yet.

**1. Read before writing**

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/<deferred-backlog reference>   # the Deferred-item schema
Read specs/deferred_items.md                                       # if it exists; append only, never overwrite
Bash: ls specs/completed/
```

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`** under `## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06`. There will be one item for the unticked stage and one for each Ranked-list item. Each item will be self-contained, with `Size:` and `Done when:`, and follow the schema exactly once I've read it:

- **Closure notices (was Stage 2, O5, Track B).** Boat operators get an email within an hour of a lock closing. It needs the closure log's live feed.
  - Size: small, based on one closure-log poll every 10 minutes.
  - Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.
- **7-day closure-risk outlook (O2, Track A, rank 1).** An outlook for each lock from the river-level forecast. It builds on Stage 1's curve: closures are rare below 3.1 m and reach about 60% at 3.8 m. That fit took 22 minutes on 1.8 GB (see `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md`).
  - Size: small, one model run a day.
  - Done when: a 7-day closure-risk outlook exists for each lock.
- **Per-lock closure curves (O3, Track A, rank 2).** Separate curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks. Stage 1 found that the four longest-record locks show nearly the same curve.
  - Size: about 14 times Stage 1's data.
  - Done when: a pooled curve exists for each of the 14 locks.
- **Closure-history map (O4, Track A, rank 3).** A closure-history map for the canal's boat operators.
  - Size: about a day of work, one static map page.
  - Done when: the map page shows each lock's closure history.

Stage 2's "text-message notices" was never a stage or list item, so nothing is parked for it.

**3. Retire the roadmap**

```
Bash: git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Edit: add under the title:  PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete
Bash: git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
      git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: funding ended; 1 of 2 stages complete, rest to deferred_items"
```

The commit goes on `main`. There is no spec, methodology or critique file to retire alongside it. Stage 1's findings file stays where it is, and the outlook and per-lock items cite it.

**One thing to check:** the session says today is 2026-11-06, but my environment says 2026-11-27. I've used 2026-11-06 in the section heading and the PARKED marker. Tell me if it should be 2026-11-27. Otherwise this is the whole park, and no stage is handed off.
